title: Plants
introductionText:
Biology
Plants
The Big Idea: A plant has four main parts and each part has a job. A seed needs water to start growing, and a plant needs water and light
to stay healthy.
Say It Like This — give every part a job
Roots — "the plant's straws". They drink water from the soil and hold the plant down so the wind cannot blow it
away.
Stem — "the plant's neck". It holds the plant up and carries the water all the way to the leaves.
Leaf — "the plant's kitchen". Leaves catch the sunlight and use it to make the plant's food.
Flower — "where the babies are made". The flower makes the seeds that grow into new plants.
Watch Out For
"The plant eats the soil"
Children think the plant sucks up food from the ground like soup. Correct it simply: "The roots drink the water. The leaves make the food
from sunlight." That is why a plant in a dark cupboard goes pale and floppy even when you water it.
Try It at Home
Activity 1 — The bean in a glass (8 days)
Push wet cotton wool into a clear glass. Slide two or three dry beans down the side of the glass so they are pressed against it and he can
watch them. Keep the cotton damp. Every morning he looks and draws what he sees.
Day 1: nothing. Day 4: a small white root pushes downwards. Day 7: a shoot pushes upwards. Day 8: the first tiny green leaves open.
Activity 2 — The light test (9 days)
Plant two young beans the same way in two pots. Put one on a sunny windowsill and one inside a dark cupboard. Water both exactly the
same. After nine days, bring them together and compare. The plant in the light is green, short and strong. The plant in the dark is pale
yellow, long, thin and floppy. He will never forget that plants need light.
Day 1 Day 4 Day 7 Day 8
nothing yet a root goes down a shoot goes up first green leaves
What he should see in the glass. Let him draw his own version each morning.
More examples to talk about
We eat different parts of plants! This one always surprises children:
• We eat the root of a carrot and a radish.
• We eat the stem of celery and sugar cane.
• We eat the leaves of lettuce, mint and parsley.
• We eat the flower of cauliflower and broccoli.
• We eat the seeds of beans, rice, lentils and peas.
Open the fridge together and sort the vegetables into these five groups.
Key Words
roots stem leaf flower petal seed grow healthy

sourceQuestions.sourceText:
Write the name of the plant part that does each job:
a) It drinks water from the soil.
b) It holds the plant up.
c) It catches the sunlight.
d) It makes the seeds.
sourceQuestions.answerKeyText: a) roots b) stem c) leaf (leaves) d) flower

sourceQuestions.sourceText: Which part of the plant comes out of the seed first? the root / the leaf
sourceQuestions.answerKeyText: The root comes first — the seed needs a drink before it can grow upwards.

sourceQuestions.sourceText: What two things does a plant need to stay healthy?
sourceQuestions.answerKeyText: Water and light. (Warmth and air are also correct if he says them.)

sourceQuestions.sourceText:
A plant was kept in a dark cupboard for nine days. Circle the words that describe it:
green pale yellow thick stem thin floppy stem healthy not healthy
sourceQuestions.answerKeyText: pale yellow, thin floppy stem, not healthy

sourceQuestions.sourceText:
True or false?
a) Seeds need water to start growing. TRUE / FALSE
b) A plant is not a living thing. TRUE / FALSE
c) Leaves make the food for the plant. TRUE / FALSE
sourceQuestions.answerKeyText: a) TRUE b) FALSE — a plant is a living thing c) TRUE

sourceQuestions.sourceText: Go on a plant hunt outside. Draw one plant you find and label its roots, stem, leaf and flower.
sourceQuestions.answerKeyText: Child's own drawing, with roots, stem, leaf and flower labelled.

sourceQuestions.sourceText: What would happen to a plant if we stopped watering it for two weeks?
sourceQuestions.answerKeyText: It would dry out: the leaves would droop and go brown, and in the end the plant would die.

sourceQuestions.sourceText: Name a vegetable where we eat the root, and one where we eat the leaves.
sourceQuestions.answerKeyText: Root: carrot, radish, beetroot. Leaves: lettuce, mint, parsley, spinach.

sourceQuestions.sourceText: The part that holds the plant up is the ( root ) ( stem ) ( flower )
Leaves make the plant's food using ( sunlight ) ( soil ) ( wind )
Seeds are made inside the ( leaf ) ( flower ) ( root )
When we eat a carrot we are eating the ( root ) ( stem ) ( flower )
A plant kept with no light will look ( green and strong ) ( pale and floppy )
